title: Delsarte linear-programming bound
statement:
Fix naturals $n$ and $d$, and let $F_0, F_1, \dots, F_n$ be real coefficients defining the function $F(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_j\, K_j^{(n)}(x)$. Suppose that $F_0 > 0$, that $F_j \ge 0$ for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$, and that $F(x) \le 0$ for every integer $x$ with $d \le x \le n$. Then the maximum size of a binary code of length $n$ and minimum distance $d$ satisfies
\[
  A(n,d) \;\le\; \frac{F(0)}{F_0}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: F(x) <= 0 for every integer x with d <= x <= n
